results.Notes: Authentic conduct-standard reasoning: the candidate must apply the indirect limb of 247 CMR 9.01(2) to the design of an arrangement rather than to its steps. Distractors are the real competing theories (step-wise legality, direct-only reading, harm, financial gain). Closest bank comparisons MA-Q-0195 (0.080) and MA-Q-0220; no pre-existing item addresses circumvention. NOTE: the option architecture (two 'no violation because' defences, two 'violation if [absent element]' conditionals, one categorical 'violation because') is shared with MA-Q-0315, and both use financial gain as a non-element; the legal content differs entirely but the scaffolding echo is recorded for the controller.

Tests a genuine practice trap: importing the remuneration element of 247 CMR 9.01(11) into 9.01(14), which has none. Scenario (pads supplied free, no agreement, no steering) is realistic and strips away every element the candidate might expect to matter. Closest bank comparison MA-Q-0143 (0.091); no pre-existing item covers blank prescription forms.

Inspection scenario is authentic and the copy-versus-original distinction is a real custody question. Distractor A is the plausible intuition that the pharmacist keeps the signed original. Sibling MA-Q-0298 (0.117) tests the dual-board retrievability and misallocated original rather than the content of the custody duty, so the pair are genuinely different applications and not cosmetic variants. Closest pre-existing MA-Q-0082 (0.129), which tests CDTM retail scope only.

Two-limb item requiring the candidate to reject both the single-board retrievability claim and the transfer of the original. Realistic: physicians do hand documents to pharmacists for safekeeping. Distinct from sibling MA-Q-0297 (0.117), which enumerates the custody duty rather than testing misallocation. Closest pre-existing MA-Q-0247 (0.119), an unrelated support-personnel documentation item.

Reasoning is from the content of the agreement rather than from the competence of the staff member, which is the authentic failure mode. Sibling MA-Q-0300 (0.161) tests the second sentence of 247 CMR 16.04(3) and is a different application. Closest pre-existing MA-Q-0294 (0.106), CDTM discipline notification, unrelated.

Requires the candidate to read past the first sentence of 247 CMR 16.04(3), a realistic drafting-review task. Distinct from sibling MA-Q-0299 (0.161), which tests whether silence permits delegation at all. Closest pre-existing MA-Q-0294 (0.164), CDTM discipline notification; different proposition and no rule shared.

Two-engagement structure mirrors how retail pharmacies actually structure physician relationships, and the discriminator is statutory PURPOSE. Distractor D (compensation unrelated to volume) is an authentic anti-kickback reflex that the statute does not adopt. Closest pre-existing MA-Q-0083 (0.123), CDTM controlled-substance limits; different rule.

Walk-in with a second-hand account of a physician's remark is a highly realistic community-pharmacy situation. Distractors A, B and D are the three plausible ways a pharmacist might wrongly self-authorise. Sibling MA-Q-0303 (0.131) tests the recording locus rather than eligibility. Closest pre-existing MA-Q-0294 (0.085).

Tests dual recording against a confident assurance from the physician that documentation is complete, which is an authentic source of pharmacist error. Distinct from sibling MA-Q-0302 (0.131). Closest pre-existing MA-Q-0294 (0.114); no overlap of proposition.

Strongest item in the tranche for setting-sensitivity: the same facts satisfy the definition of Referral in a hospital and fail it in a community pharmacy, which is exactly the distinction 243 CMR 2.12(1) draws. Parallel-scenario construction is fair and not leaky. Closest pre-existing MA-Q-0082 (0.092); no pre-existing item addresses referral meaning by setting.

Definitional inventory item, but the inclusion of the diagnosis option makes it a boundary test rather than recall. Sibling MA-Q-0306 (0.139) applies the same boundary to a fact pattern with a split outcome, which is a genuinely different cognitive task. Closest pre-existing MA-Q-0081 (0.105), CDTM qualifications.

Applies the diagnostic-component limit to facts where every ordering condition is satisfied, so the candidate cannot reason from compliance with one limb to the other. Distractor E (report to the physician) is an authentic 'cure by escalation' instinct. Distinct from sibling MA-Q-0305 (0.139). Closest pre-existing MA-Q-0083 (0.127).

Timing item with an authentic trap: a written notice is present in the plan and matches the written-notice duty, which invites the candidate to stop looking. Realistic wind-down scenario. Closest pre-existing MA-Q-0293 (0.111), CDTM continuing-education evidence; unrelated.

Pairs a permissive paper limb against a conditioned electronic limb, and the realistic detail that a flattened email image cannot be stored or retrieved is a true operational failure. Distractor B is the plausible assumption that electronic transmission is self-validating. Closest pre-existing MA-Q-0068 (0.092); no pre-existing item covers CDTM writing form.

FAIL on distinctness. The tranche item duplicates pre-existing MA-Q-0213 (lexical similarity 0.150, the highest external match for this item). MA-Q-0213 puts the same pharmacy in the same home-delivery scenario using the same toll-free service under the same sentence of M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 21A, and keys 'Print the toll-free service number on a label affixed to each prescription drug container'; MA-Q-0309 keys 'Not compliant, because the number must be on a label affixed to each container'. The two keys are the same proposition in positive and negative voice, and MA-Q-0213's distractor C (number only on the delivery receipt the patient signs) is substantially MA-Q-0309's operative fact. The item is a cosmetic reframing and adds no legal content the bank does not already establish. Legally sound but not independently releasable as a distinct item.

FAIL on distinctness. The entire proposition tested is already keyed correct in pre-existing MA-Q-0086 (lexical similarity 0.127), whose option C reads 'If there is no record that the patient failed to accept the offer, the statute creates a presumption that counseling was provided.' MA-Q-0310 makes that single sentence the whole of an SBA item under the same statute, so a candidate who has seen MA-Q-0086 obtains it without further knowledge. The counter-intuitive direction of the presumption is a genuine teaching point, but it is one the bank already carries. Legally sound; needs a materially different application to be releasable.

Constitutive-elements item where the Board-filing distractor is an authentic analogy to licensure processes that do require filing. Closest pre-existing MA-Q-0294 (0.138) and MA-Q-0292 (CDTM prescriptive practice conditions), both testing different CDTM propositions; no rule shared.

Excellent construction: two pharmacists reaching opposite conclusions forces the candidate to separate 'named' from 'current', which are independent axes. Neither keyed option can be reached by elimination alone. Closest pre-existing MA-Q-0221 (0.078); no pre-existing item addresses DUR evidentiary basis.

FAIL on distinctness. The sole proposition tested, that measures taken in response to a drug utilization review must be documented, is already keyed correct in pre-existing MA-Q-0085 (lexical similarity 0.134), whose option E reads 'Take appropriate measures to resolve an identified therapy problem, which may include consultation with the prescriber or patient and documentation of the measures taken.' MA-Q-0313 isolates the trailing documentation clause of that keyed option and makes it the whole item, adding no legal content beyond it. The 'clinically resolved therefore file closed' framing is a presentation device rather than new law. Legally sound; requires a genuinely new discriminator to be releasable.

Sterile versus non-sterile boundary is a real and consequential distinction, and the two-refusal structure makes the candidate apply the duty's scope rather than a general attitude to compounding. Distractor E (another nearby pharmacy) is an authentic but wrong equitable instinct. Closest pre-existing MA-Q-0228 (0.074); no pre-existing item covers refusal to compound.

Strips the scenario of every element candidates expect to matter (accuracy, no companion breach, no reliance, no loss) so that only the freestanding character of 247 CMR 9.01(9) resolves it. NOTE: shares option architecture with MA-Q-0295, including the use of financial gain as a non-element distractor; the rules and legal content are entirely different but the scaffolding echo is recorded for the controller. Closest pre-existing MA-Q-0195 (0.080).

Authentic workflow exposure (prescriptions face up, visible waiting list) rather than a disclosure hypothetical, which is what makes the affirmative protective limb bite. Distractor C is a realistic confusion with the consultation-area requirement. Closest pre-existing MA-Q-0285 (0.089) tests consultation-area accessibility, a different proposition.

Two returns on the same afternoon is a clean way to test mandatory against discretionary acceptance. PARTIAL OVERLAP recorded: pre-existing MA-Q-0088 (0.143) already keys 'Accept the return because it was previously dispensed in error', but MA-Q-0088 contains only an error return and tests post-acceptance quarantine and disposal; the discretionary limb for a properly dispensed, non-defective return is new to the bank and is this item's actual discriminator. Distinct on balance.

Both duties are tested against a realistic stock-out, and option E correctly makes inability to supply the trigger rather than an excuse. Closest pre-existing MA-Q-0225 (0.093) and MA-Q-0111 (Schedule II/III consumer pamphlet), neither of which concerns the opioid antagonist pamphlet or referral duties.

Purchaser-versus-user billing with a timing limb is a genuine operational decision and the intuitive answer (bill the user) is wrong. NOTE: the scenario template closely echoes pre-existing MA-Q-0097 (0.118), which also features a parent obtaining naloxone for an absent adult child; however MA-Q-0097 tests whether third-party access is lawful at all, while this item tests whose coverage is billed and when, under M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 19B(e). Different proposition, no rule shared; the scenario echo is recorded for the controller.

Two-pharmacy comparison isolates effort from outcome, which is precisely how the reasonable-effort standard operates, and the stem forecloses the significance escape route by holding the gap identical. Closest pre-existing MA-Q-0019 (0.099); MA-Q-0086 keys recording a counselling refusal, a different application of the same standard.

Employer pressure against individual competence is an authentic and consequential pharmacist decision, and the conjunctive reading of 247 CMR 9.01(4) is the whole point. Distractor C (observed by a trained colleague) is a realistic workaround that the regulation does not recognise. Closest pre-existing MA-Q-0171 (0.071), the lowest external maximum in the tranche.

Realistic staffing failure with genuine patient need, and the item requires the candidate to carry the minimisation and documentation conditions along with the exception rather than treating patient interest as sufficient. Sibling MA-Q-0323 (0.101) tests the rest period rather than the conditions for exceeding, so the pair are different limbs. Closest pre-existing MA-Q-0229 (0.066).

Broken rest with an intervening shift in an unrelated setting is a realistic and precise way to test 'consecutive', and the documented extenuating circumstance is an authentic distractor because it legitimated the prior shift. Distinct from sibling MA-Q-0322 (0.101). Closest pre-existing MA-Q-0294 (0.114); MA-Q-0078 concerns intern hours, a different provision.

Colleague-assertion framing carries two independent errors and the candidate must reject both. PARTIAL OVERLAP recorded: option C restates a proposition already keyed in pre-existing MA-Q-0085 (0.101) option C, but the item's discriminating content, that the statutory screening list is illustrative and that over-the-counter interactions are expressly within it, is new to the bank. Distinct on balance.

Best mandatory-versus-permissive contrast in the tranche, drawn between two adjacent standing-order regimes where candidates reasonably expect uniformity. Realistic weekly planning frame. Closest pre-existing MA-Q-0137 (0.090); no pre-existing item contrasts standing-order training preconditions.

Three-way sort by recipient status is authentic disposal decision-making and the sympathetic aid-group option is a well-judged distractor. Distinct from pre-existing MA-Q-0071 (0.099) and MA-Q-0130, which test federal DEA reverse-distributor registration and Form 41 destruction records rather than the Massachusetts recipient-authorisation limit in 247 CMR 9.01(12).

Two-point structure tests both limbs of 247 CMR 9.01(3), currency and Board displacement, and resists the common all-or-nothing view of USP authority. The dusty binder detail is realistic. Closest pre-existing MA-Q-0293 (0.071); MA-Q-0214 concerns hazardous-drug handling standards, a different proposition.
